name: Khongjom War Memorial Complex
description: Memorial complex on Kheba Ching hill in Khongjom, Thoubal district, commemorating the decisive Battle of Khongjom (23 April 1891) during the Anglo-Manipur War. Features a tall sword monument, gardens, and tributes to Manipuri warriors including Major Paona Brajabasi who resisted British forces.
facts: Site of the last major battle of the Anglo-Manipur War of 1891
About 32-36 km southeast of Imphal on NH-102
Hosts annual Khongjom Day observances on 23 April
Includes world's tallest sword statue according to local sources
Tourist home functioning since 1988

name: Senapati Town
description: District headquarters of Senapati (also known as Tahamzam), a hill town on NH-2 about 62 km north of Imphal, serving as gateway to northern Manipur hills with mixed ethnic communities including Mao, Maram and Poumai Nagas.
facts: Named after Tikendrajit Singh (Senapati); local name Tahamzam means 'Hill of Butterflies'
Elevation around 1500 m
On National Highway 2 linking Imphal to Nagaland

name: Willong Khullen Megaliths
description: Prehistoric megalithic site in Willong Khullen village, Mao-Maram area of Senapati district, featuring over 100-130 standing stones up to 7 m high, often compared to Stonehenge. Erected by ancient Maram Naga clans for warrior feats and feasts of merit.
facts: About 37 km from Maram on Maram-Peren Road
One of the largest megalithic complexes in Northeast India
Village is traditional Maram Naga settlement

name: Makhel Village
description: Sacred ancestral village in Senapati district believed to be the dispersal point of Naga tribes. Features sacred banyan trees (said to grow from Naga mother's tomb), farewell monolith, triomonolith, hailstorm stone and other historical monuments.
facts: Near Tadubi; sacred for multiple ethnic communities
Dispersal Tree at nearby Sajouba
Important for anthropologists studying Naga migration

name: Mao Gate
description: Historic border town and gateway on the Manipur-Nagaland boundary in Senapati district at about 1788 m elevation. Oldest hill station in the area, commercial stop on NH-2 with scenic hills and traditional Mao Naga culture.
facts: Northern entry point to Manipur from Nagaland
Base for treks to Dzuko Valley from Manipur side
Multi-ethnic commercial hub

name: Dzuko Valley (Manipur Side)
description: High-altitude valley (around 2450 m) straddling the Manipur-Nagaland border in Senapati and Kohima districts. Famous for rolling meadows, seasonal Dzuko lily (Lilium chitrangadae), wildflowers, and trekking. Manipur access from Mao/Mount Iso area.
facts: Shared with Nagaland; boundary disputed
Snow in winter, lily blooms in summer
Highest peak of Manipur Mount Iso (Tenipu) nearby

name: Maram Khullen
description: One of the largest and oldest traditional villages of the Maram Naga tribe in Senapati district. Preserves hereditary chieftainship, carved wooden houses, terraced fields and indigenous crafts; origin point of the Barak River.
facts: About 18 km from Senapati town
Attracts anthropologists
Traditional social structure intact

name: Purul Village
description: Traditional Poumai Naga village (also Hiimai Phii) in Senapati, known for indigenous games like Toutou and wrestling during festivals, stone steps and cultural heritage. Home to Poula language speakers.
facts: About 19-20 km from Maram on NH-2
Elevation around 1867 m
Consists of Purul Akutpa and Atongba

name: Yangkhullen Village
description: Historic hilltop village in Senapati district built on a steep incline, traditional Zeme or related Naga settlement with preserved lifestyle, natural beauty and cultural significance.
facts: Listed as places of interest on official district site
About 26-75 km depending on route from Senapati
Traditional architecture on steep terrain

name: Dziiduri Highland
description: Emerging eco-tourism highland at ~1960 m in Paomata block near Khumai (Tunggam) village, Senapati. Features wetland, Dziitrulai Waterfall, Abulya Cliff, sacred Natousalai site, views of Mount Iso, terraced fields and developing trekking infrastructure.
facts: Promoted as state eco-tourism gem
Views of Manipur's highest peak
Community-led development by KYSO and HEAT-M

name: Naamai Zho Eco Tourism Park
description: Scenic grassland and eco-tourism site near Koide village in Senapati, famous for cosmos flower blooms and annual Cosmos Flower Festival. Offers viewpoints and nature photography amid paddy fields and hills.
facts: Hosts Cosmos Flower Festival attracting thousands
About 5-6 km from Maram Bazar
Adopted home to colorful cosmos flowers
